focused_acceptance.reason: Proposition 10.5 permits arbitrary real polynomial coefficients. For ell=2, f_m(z)=product_{r=0}^{m-1}(1-z/2^r) vanishes at every specified node, has |a_m|=2^(-m(m-1)/2), and admits B<e*2^(m(m+1)/2). The proposed B contribution divided by this coefficient is <e*2^(-m^2/2+C*m), tending to zero for every proposed universal C; choose a positive epsilon whose contribution is at most one quarter of the actual coefficient. The signed product in z^2 analogously gives <exp(1/3)*2^(-m^2+C*m). No positivity/probability restriction excludes these examples. The convolution step loses the claimed i-dependent factor. Theorem 2.14 explicitly invokes this proposition on PDF page 61, supporting Major. A weaker coefficient bound without that factor is locally proved; complete arithmetic propagation and final constants remain unverified.
